questions.prompt: Revenue ${R}, total costs ${C}. Profit margin (%)?
questions.explanation: (${R} − ${C}) ÷ ${R} = {ANSWER:pct}.

questions.prompt: Fixed costs ${F}/month; price ${p}; variable cost ${v}/unit. Break-even units (round up)?
questions.explanation: ${F} ÷ (${p} − ${v}) → {ANSWER:int} units.

questions.prompt: Same business: fixed ${F}, price ${p}, variable ${v}. Profit at {q} units?
Which is a VARIABLE cost for a bubble-tea shop?
questions.explanation: Variable costs rise with each unit sold.

questions.prompt: Gross margin: revenue ${R}, cost of goods sold ${G}. Gross margin (%)?
questions.explanation: (${R} − ${G}) ÷ ${R} = {ANSWER:pct}.

questions.prompt: A business is profitable on paper but can't pay its suppliers this month. This is a…
questions.explanation: Customers may pay later (receivables) while bills are due now. Cash flow timing matters.

questions.prompt: Assets = Liabilities + ?
questions.explanation: The accounting equation: what you own is funded by what you owe plus what owners own.

questions.prompt: Assets ${A}; liabilities ${L}. Owner's equity?
questions.explanation: ${A} − ${L} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: A ${E} oven lasts {n} years with no resale value. Straight-line depreciation per year?
questions.explanation: ${E} ÷ {n} = ${ANSWER} per year shows up as an expense.

questions.prompt: Buying a $12,000 delivery van should be recorded as…
choices: An asset, depreciated over its life
Revenue for the month it is bought
A liability only, until it is paid off
questions.explanation: Long-lived equipment is capitalized as an asset; its cost is spread out through depreciation.

questions.prompt: Income statement: revenue ${R}, COGS ${G}, wages ${W}, rent ${T}. Net income?
A business earns ${P}/year profit and sells at {m}× earnings. Sale price?
questions.explanation: {m} × ${P} = ${ANSWER}. Valuation multiples reflect growth and risk.

questions.prompt: Hiring a worker costs ${w}/month and increases sales by ${s}/month. Your margin on extra sales is {m}%. Monthly gain or loss from hiring?
questions.explanation: Extra profit = ${s} × {m}% − ${w} = ${ANSWER}. Hire only if positive.

questions.prompt: You invest ${I} to start a business that profits ${P}/month. Simple payback period (months)?
questions.explanation: ${I} ÷ ${P} = {ANSWER} months.

questions.prompt: Return on investment: you put in ${I} and earned ${P} profit over the year. ROI (%)?
questions.explanation: ${P} ÷ ${I} = {ANSWER:pct}. Compare with what an index fund might earn for less risk.

questions.prompt: Demand falls when price rises. This is the…
questions.explanation: Higher prices → lower quantity demanded (all else equal).

questions.prompt: Demand is Q = {a} − {b}×P. At a price of ${p}, how many units are demanded?
questions.explanation: {a} − {b} × {p} = {ANSWER:int}.

questions.prompt: Demand Q = {a} − {b}P. Revenue = P × Q. Which price maximizes revenue? (P = a / (2b))
questions.explanation: Revenue P(a − bP) peaks at P = a/(2b) = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: A storm cuts the supply of cargo ships. Shipping prices will likely…
questions.explanation: Lower supply with the same demand raises prices.

questions.prompt: A tariff is…
questions.explanation: Tariffs make imports more expensive, often raising prices for consumers.

questions.prompt: A ${p} imported gadget gets a {t}% tariff, fully passed on to buyers. New price?
Comparative advantage means a city should specialize in what it can produce…
choices: In the largest amount, whatever the cost
questions.explanation: Even if one place is better at everything, both gain by specializing where their opportunity cost is lowest and trading.

questions.prompt: Trade: buy {n} units at ${b}, ship for ${s} total, sell at ${p}. Profit?
Selling 200 units into a small market drops the price from $20 to $14. This is called…
questions.explanation: Big sales relative to demand push prices down; spreading sales across markets can earn more.

questions.prompt: In perfect competition, many sellers offer identical goods. Who sets the price?
choices: The market: each seller is a price taker
Each customer bargains a personal price
questions.explanation: With many identical sellers, no one can charge more than the market price.

questions.prompt: A monopoly typically leads to…
questions.explanation: Without competitors, a monopolist can restrict output and charge more.

questions.prompt: Price ${p}, variable cost ${v}. Contribution margin ratio (%)?
questions.explanation: (${p} − ${v}) ÷ ${p} = {ANSWER:pct}.

questions.prompt: Target profit ${T}; fixed costs ${F}; price ${p}; variable ${v}. Units needed?
questions.explanation: (${T} + ${F}) ÷ (${p} − ${v}) → {ANSWER:int} units.

questions.prompt: Accounts receivable are…
questions.explanation: Receivables are an asset; payables (owed to suppliers) are a liability.

questions.prompt: Find the error: 'Rent $2,000' appears twice in one month's expenses. Effect on reported profit?
questions.explanation: A duplicate expense makes profit look $2,000 lower than it really is.

questions.prompt: Inventory: start ${a}, purchases ${b}, end ${c}. Cost of goods sold (COGS)?
questions.explanation: COGS = beginning + purchases − ending = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities. Current assets ${a}, current liabilities ${l}. Ratio?
questions.explanation: ${a} ÷ ${l} = {ANSWER}. Below 1 can signal trouble paying near-term bills.

questions.prompt: Pricing strategy: setting a low price to win customers, then raising it later is called…
questions.explanation: Penetration pricing trades early margin for market share. Skimming starts high then lowers.

questions.prompt: Delivery: {d} orders × ${f} fee + ${t} average tip, minus {m} meters × ${c}/meter fuel. Profit?
Which business structure protects the owner's personal savings from business debts?
choices: None of them can protect you
questions.explanation: Limited liability separates business debts from personal assets (with some exceptions).

questions.prompt: A stronger Hong Kong dollar makes Hong Kong's exports…
questions.explanation: A stronger currency raises the foreign price of exports.

questions.prompt: Each extra dumpling costs ${c} to make. Customers will pay ${p}. Fixed rent ${F}/night. Minimum dumplings to avoid a loss (round up)?
questions.explanation: ${F} ÷ (${p} − ${c}) → {ANSWER:int}.

questions.prompt: Your stall sells out every night by 8pm. What does that tell you?
choices: Demand beats supply: make more or charge more
Lower the price to attract more people
Close the stall, it’s too much work
questions.explanation: Selling out means you're leaving money on the table.

questions.prompt: Price rises from ${a} to ${b}; quantity sold falls from {q1} to {q2}. Arc elasticity ≈ (%ΔQ)/(%ΔP) using midpoints. Value (positive)?
questions.explanation: Midpoint %ΔQ ÷ %ΔP = {ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Revenue minus all expenses equals…
questions.explanation: Net income is the bottom line.

questions.prompt: Monthly profits for a food cart: ${a}, ${b}, ${c}. Average monthly profit?
Seasonal businesses (like summer bubble tea) should…
choices: Save cash in strong months for slow ones
Spend all the profit during the summer
Borrow every winter without a plan
Ignore seasons and keep costs fixed
questions.explanation: Cash reserves smooth out seasonal swings.

questions.prompt: GDP measures…
choices: The value of all goods and services made
How much the government has borrowed
The average price of listed stocks
How fast consumer prices are rising
questions.explanation: Gross domestic product sums the value of final goods and services.

questions.prompt: Real GDP growth ≈ nominal growth − inflation. Nominal GDP grew {n}%, inflation {i}%. Approximate real growth (%)?
questions.explanation: {n}% − {i}% ≈ {ANSWER:pct}.

questions.prompt: Two competing stalls both cut prices again and again. The likely outcome is…
choices: A price war that shrinks both profits
Both stalls get rich from volume
Prices end up higher than before
questions.explanation: Price wars benefit customers but can wipe out sellers' margins.

questions.prompt: Markup: cost ${c}, selling price ${p}. Markup on cost (%)?
questions.explanation: (${p} − ${c}) ÷ ${c} = {ANSWER:pct} markup (different from margin, which divides by price).

questions.prompt: Cash flow statement: buying equipment appears under…
questions.explanation: Operating = day-to-day; investing = long-term assets; financing = loans and owners' money.

questions.prompt: Taking a business loan appears on the cash flow statement under…
questions.explanation: Borrowing and repaying loans are financing cash flows.

questions.prompt: Higher interest rates usually affect small businesses by…
questions.explanation: Costlier borrowing can delay expansion and reduce demand.

questions.prompt: Customer acquisition cost ${a}; each customer brings ${m} profit per month and stays {n} months. Lifetime profit minus acquisition cost?
questions.explanation: ${m} × {n} − ${a} = ${ANSWER}. If negative, marketing loses money.

questions.prompt: Exports minus imports is called the…
questions.explanation: A positive trade balance is a surplus; negative is a deficit.

questions.prompt: Weekly sales ${s} at a {m}% net margin. Weekly profit?
questions.explanation: ${s} × {m}% = ${ANSWER}.
